classification.difficultyReason: Constructs two time-dependent positions and solves a squared-distance equality while retaining the initial-time solution.

inlines.text: Jane stands at a fixed point
, and arrives there after 1 hour. Mary starts at the same time from
and drives along the same line, but twice as fast.
Assume both travel at constant speed. Let
be time (hours) from when Bob starts driving. Consider only
, from their common departure until Mary first reaches

answer.short:
At $t=0$, both are at $(0,8)$. At $t=\tfrac12$ hour, Bob is at $(4,4)$ and Mary is at $(8,0)$.

Form their parametric positions and equate squared distances from Jane.
answer.worked:
Using the uniform-speed model, with $t$ in hours and $0\leq t\leq\tfrac12$,
$$\begin{align*}B(t)&=(8t,8-8t)\\M(t)&=(16t,8-16t).\end{align*}$$
Their squared distances from $J(-4,-8)$ are
$$\begin{align*}JB^2&=(8t+4)^2+(16-8t)^2\\JB^2&=128t^2-192t+272\\JM^2&=(16t+4)^2+(16-16t)^2\\JM^2&=512t^2-384t+272.\end{align*}$$
Equating these gives
$$\begin{align*}128t^2-192t+272&=512t^2-384t+272\\192t(2t-1)&=0\\t&=0\text{ or }\frac12.\end{align*}$$
Both times lie in the specified interval. At $t=0$, both are at $(0,8)$. At $t=\tfrac12$ hour, Bob is at $(4,4)$ and Mary is at $(8,0)$.
